issues.t: Head gasket failure linked to oil cooler and EGR cooler problems
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, coolant is pushed out of the overflow bottle, white smoke from the exhaust, overheating when towing, or engine temperature that climbs on hills.
issues.why: On the 6.0L diesel, the engine oil cooler clogs and starves the EGR cooler of coolant flow. The EGR cooler then cracks and leaks coolant, and the stock head bolts can let combustion pressure push past the head gaskets, especially under heavy towing.
issues.next: Stop towing and get it checked before you overheat it again. Ask a diesel shop to compare oil and coolant temperatures and pressure-test the cooling system. Catching a clogged oil cooler early can prevent head gasket damage.

issues.t: Major engine failure or sudden power loss on the 6.4L diesel
issues.sym: The truck suddenly loses power, often while towing, or runs rough and won't make power. Some owners were told the whole engine needed replacing.
issues.why: The 6.4L diesel is known for serious problems: fuel and water reaching the high-pressure fuel system, cracked exhaust parts, cooling system leaks and fuel thinning the oil. When these are ignored the engine can be badly damaged.
issues.next: If power drops while towing, pull over safely and stop. Have a diesel specialist scan for codes and check the fuel-water separator, oil level and coolant level before replacing big parts.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump (CP4) failure
issues.sym: The truck stalls or loses power and then cranks but won't start. Repairs are often major because metal debris spreads through the fuel system.
issues.why: The Bosch CP4 high-pressure pump on the 6.7L diesel can wear internally, and many technicians blame low lubricity in US diesel fuel or water in the fuel. Metal flakes then travel to the injectors and fuel lines.
issues.next: Have it towed rather than cranking it over and over. Ask the shop to check the fuel filters for metal. Change both fuel filters on time and drain water from the separator to lower the risk.

issues.t: Fuel injector failure on the 6.0L diesel
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfire, smoke, hard starting or loss of power, sometimes after a long period of running fine.
issues.why: 6.0L injectors are sensitive to fuel quality, oil condition and weak batteries feeding the injector control module. When injectors stick or wear, the engine misfires and can wash fuel into the oil.
issues.next: Get a diesel shop to run an injector balance and contribution test before replacing parts. Test the batteries and the injector control module voltage too, because a weak module can make good injectors act up.

issues.t: Spark plug blown out of the cylinder head
issues.sym: A sudden loud popping or ticking like a tapping hammer, rough running and a misfire on one cylinder. You may see the coil pack lifted or hear exhaust puffing from under the hood.
issues.why: The 5.4L and 6.8L V10 gas engines in these trucks have very few threads holding each spark plug in the aluminum head. Over time a plug can work loose and shoot out, stripping the threads.
issues.next: Stop driving it to avoid more damage, since it will run poorly and can damage the coil. A shop can usually repair the threads with an insert without removing the head. When plugs are changed, make sure they are torqued correctly.

issues.t: Turbocharger failure on early 6.7L diesels
issues.sym: A loud screech or whine from the engine, blue or gray smoke from burning oil, and loss of power.
issues.why: Early 6.7L diesels used a turbo with ceramic ball bearings that could fail. Ford later moved to a steel-bearing design.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear screeching or see heavy smoke, because a failing turbo can send parts into the engine. Have a diesel shop inspect the turbo for shaft play and oil leaks.

issues.t: Radiator leaks at the end tanks on the 6.4L diesel
issues.sym: Puddles of coolant under the front of the truck, a sweet smell, or the coolant level dropping between checks.
issues.why: The crimped seams that hold the plastic end tanks to the radiator core loosen over time, mostly on early-build trucks, and start to seep coolant.
issues.next: Check the coolant level often and don't let it run low, because overheating can badly damage a diesel. Replace the radiator when it starts leaking and pressure-test the rest of the system.

issues.t: Fuel thinning the engine oil during DPF cleaning
issues.sym: The oil level on the dipstick keeps going up, the oil smells like diesel, and fuel economy drops.
issues.why: To clean its diesel particulate filter (DPF), the 6.4L injects extra fuel late in each cycle. Some of that fuel slips past the piston rings into the oil, thinning it. Short trips and long idling make it worse.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and change the oil sooner than the normal interval if it's rising. Use low-ash diesel oil and ultra-low-sulfur diesel. Highway runs let the DPF clean itself more completely.

issues.t: Fuel tank lining flakes and clogs the fuel filter
issues.sym: The truck loses power or stalls, especially under load, and fuel filters clog again soon after being changed. Shops may find gray flakes in the filter.
issues.why: The coating inside the steel diesel fuel tank on these heavy-duty Ford trucks can separate and peel. The flakes clog the filter and can damage the fuel pump and injectors.
issues.next: If the fuel filter clogs often, ask the shop to inspect it for flakes. Replacing the tank, often with an aftermarket plastic tank, plus new filters, stops it coming back.

issues.t: Camshaft position sensor can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls without warning while driving, or cranks but won't start, often when hot. The tachometer may drop to zero just before it dies.
issues.why: The camshaft position sensor on the 7.3L diesel can work only some of the time. When it drops out, the engine loses its timing signal and shuts off.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Treat an unexpected stall as a safety problem. Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer replaces the sensor with an improved part for free.

issues.t: Speed control deactivation switch can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke near the brake master cylinder on the driver's side of the engine bay, or cruise control that stops working. A fire can start even with the engine off.
issues.why: The cruise control shut-off switch near the brake master cylinder can leak brake fluid internally, then overheat and burn.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. If you smell burning or see smoke, park outside away from buildings. Check your VIN; the dealer adds a fused wiring harness for free. Ford recommends parking outside until it's done.

issues.t: Automatic transmission failure
issues.sym: Slipping, harsh or delayed shifts, loss of second gear, fluid leaks, or the truck refusing to move. Some owners had a second failure on the replacement unit.
issues.why: The heavy-duty 4-speed automatic in these trucks wears out early under towing and heavy loads, and seal leaks can let it run low on fluid and burn up.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell for burnt fluid. If it slips, stop towing and get it diagnosed before it fails completely. An extra transmission cooler helps trucks that tow often.

issues.t: 4x4 front hubs won't lock or unlock
issues.sym: Four-wheel drive doesn't engage, or the front hubs stay locked when they shouldn't, causing grinding or binding. The plastic hub caps can crack.
issues.why: These trucks use vacuum-operated automatic locking hubs. Cracked plastic hub parts, vacuum leaks and worn bearings stop them from working as designed.
issues.next: Have the vacuum lines and hub assemblies checked. Many owners switch to manual locking hubs for reliability. Don't count on 4x4 in snow or off-road until it's fixed.

issues.t: Driveshaft damper can slip and break the driveshaft (recall)
issues.sym: A vibration or clunk from under the truck that gets worse, then a sudden loss of power to the wheels. The truck may roll in Park if the parking brake isn't set.
issues.why: On 4x4 trucks, a ring-shaped damper on the rear driveshaft can shift. That unbalances the driveshaft until it breaks.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake when parked. Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and repairs the driveshaft for free.

issues.t: Underbody insulator can wear through the aluminum driveshaft (recall)
issues.sym: Rubbing or scraping noises from under the cab, then vibration. If the driveshaft breaks, the truck suddenly loses drive power.
issues.why: On gas-engine trucks with an aluminum driveshaft, underbody heat or sound insulators can come loose and rub on the spinning driveshaft until it fractures.
issues.next: Check your VIN. The dealer inspects the driveshaft, replaces it if damaged, and reattaches the insulators for free.

issues.t: Dana 275 rear axle housing can bend and drop the driveshaft (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks or vibration from the rear, especially after heavy towing, then a sudden loss of drive power. The truck may roll if left in Park without the parking brake.
issues.why: On F-350 diesel trucks with the Dana 275 rear axle, the axle housing can deform under load. That can let the driveshaft separate from the axle.
issues.next: Set the parking brake every time you park. Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and repairs the axle for free. Avoid heavy towing until it's checked.

issues.t: Dual rear wheel front hub extenders can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking, wobble or vibration from a front wheel on a dually. In the worst case a front wheel can come off.
issues.why: Dual rear wheel F-350s use hub extenders on the front wheels so they line up with the wide rear wheels. The fasteners holding the extenders may not be tight enough.
issues.next: Ford tells owners not to drive these trucks until they are fixed. Check your VIN and have the truck towed to a dealer if the recall is open.

issues.t: Fifth-wheel hitch bracket can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Creaking or clunking from the bed when towing a fifth-wheel or gooseneck trailer, or visible cracks near the left-side hitch mount.
issues.why: On some 2021 F-350s with the factory fifth-wheel prep, the left mounting bracket can crack, so the hitch could come loose while towing.
issues.next: Don't tow a fifth-wheel or gooseneck trailer until the recall is checked. Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and replaces the bracket for free.

issues.t: Left rear axle shaft may break (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding or clunking from the rear wheel, then a sudden loss of drive. The truck could roll away in Park without the parking brake.
issues.why: On 2023 single rear wheel trucks, the left rear axle shaft may not have been heat-treated correctly and can snap.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time you park. Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and replaces the axle shaft for free.

issues.t: Rear driveshaft weld can fail (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or vibration from under the truck followed by a sudden loss of power to the wheels.
issues.why: A friction weld on the rear driveshaft may not be strong enough and can separate.
issues.next: Set the parking brake when parked. Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and replaces the driveshaft for free.

issues.t: Right rear axle shaft may break (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding or clunking from the rear wheel, then a sudden loss of drive power, or the truck rolling in Park.
issues.why: The right rear axle shaft may not have been heat-treated properly and can break.
issues.next: Set the parking brake every time you park. Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and replaces the axle shaft for free.

issues.t: Truck can briefly move in reverse when shifted to Drive (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift from Park to Drive, the truck lurches backward for a second or two even though the display shows D.
issues.why: A transmission software fault on some early-build 2015 trucks with the 6R140 automatic can engage Reverse for about 1.5 seconds.
issues.next: Keep your foot firmly on the brake when shifting. Check your VIN; the dealer updates the transmission software for free.

issues.t: Violent front-end shake ('death wobble')
issues.sym: After hitting a bump or expansion joint at highway speed, the steering wheel and front end shake violently and won't stop until you slow way down.
issues.why: The solid front axle uses a track bar, ball joints and a steering damper. Wear, loose parts, caster settings or out-of-balance tires let the front wheels start oscillating, and the motion feeds on itself.
issues.next: Firmly hold the wheel and slow down gradually; don't slam the brakes. Have the track bar, ball joints, tie rods, steering damper and alignment checked. Ask the dealer about Ford's steering damper program and service bulletins for your year.

issues.t: Fast or uneven front tire wear
issues.sym: The front tires wear out much faster than expected, often on the edges, and may need replacing well before 40,000 miles.
issues.why: Heavy front ends, worn steering parts and alignment settings that drift out of spec cause the front tires to scrub.
issues.next: Rotate tires on schedule and get an alignment check, especially after hitting potholes or after any death-wobble repair.

issues.t: Steering column upper shaft can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Loose or vague steering, clunks in the steering wheel, or the wheel turning without the truck responding.
issues.why: The upper steering column shaft can detach from the rest of the column, which can cause a loss of steering.
issues.next: If the steering feels loose, stop driving and have it towed. Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and repairs it for free.

issues.t: Steering column shaft bolts may be loose or missing (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or play in the steering wheel, or steering that feels disconnected.
issues.why: On some 2023 trucks, bolts joining the upper steering column shaft were left loose or not installed, so the column can come apart.
issues.next: Don't ignore a loose-feeling steering wheel. Check your VIN; the dealer tightens or installs the bolts for free.

issues.t: Brake booster pushrod clip may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels odd or suddenly goes soft, and braking power drops.
issues.why: A retaining clip on the brake booster pushrod may be missing, so the pushrod can come apart from the brake pedal.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Ford tells owners not to drive these trucks until repaired. Check your VIN and have it towed to a dealer if the recall is open.

issues.t: Trailer brakes or trailer lights can cut out (recall)
issues.sym: A trailer brake warning on the dash, or the trailer's brakes, brake lights or turn signals stop working while towing.
issues.why: The integrated trailer brake module can lose communication with the truck because of a software problem, cutting trailer braking or lights.
issues.next: If the warning appears while towing, slow down, leave extra stopping distance and pull over safely. Check your VIN; the fix is a free software update from the dealer or over the air.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump can fail from biodiesel deposits (recall)
issues.sym: The engine loses power or stalls while driving, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: Deposits from biodiesel blends can build up in the 6.7L diesel's high-pressure fuel pump and make it fail. A first repair was not done correctly on some trucks, so Ford issued a follow-up recall.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls; the dealer updates engine and transmission software for free. If power drops, pull over safely and have it checked.

issues.t: DEF tank heater or DEF system fault
issues.sym: A check engine or DEF warning, sometimes with code P20BA, and a countdown that limits speed if not fixed.
issues.why: The heater inside the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) tank, which keeps the fluid from freezing, can fail. The truck then can't run its emissions system correctly.
issues.next: Don't ignore the warning, because the truck may go into reduced speed mode. Have a shop read the codes; the heater is usually replaced with the DEF tank sending unit.

issues.t: Tailgate can open on its own (recall)
issues.sym: The tailgate drops open while driving or parked, and cargo can fall out.
issues.why: Water can get into the electric tailgate release switch and short it, unlatching the tailgate.
issues.next: Strap down loads until fixed. Check your VIN; the dealer rewires and replaces the switch for free.

issues.t: Seat belt pretensioner can start a fire in the door pillar (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or burning smell inside the cab, usually after a crash or minor impact that fires the seat belt pretensioner.
issues.why: On Crew Cab trucks, sparks from the front seat belt pretensioner can ignite carpet or insulation inside the B-pillar.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN; the dealer adds heat-resistant tape and insulation changes for free.

issues.t: Water in tailgate module blanks the backup camera (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera image flickers or turns blue or black when in Reverse.
issues.why: Water can get into the tailgate park-assist module, disrupting the rear camera signal.
issues.next: Use mirrors and look behind you until fixed. Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the camera, harness and module for free.

issues.t: Backup camera image freezes or is delayed (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture is delayed, freezes or stays blank when you shift into Reverse.
issues.why: A software error in the module that handles the camera feed can stop the image from showing correctly.
issues.next: Back up carefully using mirrors until updated. Check your VIN; the fix is a free software update from the dealer or over the air.

issues.t: Instrument cluster may go blank or gauges stick (recall)
issues.sym: The dash may not light up at startup, so you can't see speed or warning lights, or the analog speedometer and tachometer needles stick or jump.
issues.why: Software and hardware problems in the instrument cluster can stop it from starting up properly or make the gauges read wrong.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Don't drive if the cluster is blank, because you won't see warnings. Check your VIN; Ford provides a software update and, for the gauge issue, a new cluster.
